newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves, customer or system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves, customer or system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve was expected by analysts to intervene in the banking system Tuesday morning via a round of customer or multi-day system repurchase agreements.

Analysts also warned the Fed was likely to enter the system earlier than usual -- perhaps by 1030 EST/1530 GMT -- in light of the abbreviated Christmas Eve trading session. The market was scheduled to close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
Fed funds opened at the Fed's target rate of 5-1/4 percent and have traded at that level thus far this session.

Analysts said the Fed faced a substantial add need before the end of the year and that the two outstanding 14-day fixed-term system RPs were unlikely large enough to handle that need. Marc Wanshel, economist at J.P. Morgan & Co, estimated the outstanding 14-day RPs totaled about $12 billion -- shy of his estimate of a total add need of $14 billion to $15 billion for the current maintenance period as a whole.
The end of the year and end of the current maintenance period both occur next Tuesday.
-- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663
